To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
any permutation on a circuit switched d-cube can be realized using at most d2d edges and any permutation on a packet-switch-ed d-cube can also be realized in at most 2d−3 steps.
any given permutation on the d-cube can be realized in d steps on the circuit-switched d-cubes and d2d edges on the packet-switched d-dimension hypercube.

(1) any permutation on the d-cube can be 2-realized using d2d edges, (2) any permutation on a packet-switching d-cube can 2-realized in 2d steps, and (3) the number of edges used by the 2-realization is optimal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: given a permutation on a d-cube, what is the minimum number of steps required to realize the given permutation?
the realization of an arbitrary permutation on a circuit- or packet-switched d-dimensional cube.
a fundamental problem of interconnection networks: how to realize an arbitrary permutation in the most efficient manner possible.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the total number (not counting repetitions) of directed edges used by any realization for a permutation on a circuit switched d-cube is bounded by d(d−1), and the same bound holds true for packet-switched d-dimension hypercube.
the problem of realizing an arbitrary permutation on a d-cube is solvable in 2d−3 time steps on a packet-switching model, and is solvable in d2d time steps on a circuit-switching model.
the problem of realizing an arbitrary permutation on an n×n packet-switched hypercube (n⩾3) in the minimum number of steps is solved, with the optimal bound of 2n−4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
any given permutation on an n-processor circuit-switched d-cubes can be realized in at most 3n−2 steps.
we have constructed the first explicit combinatorial 2-realization algorithm for arbitrary permutation on a d-cube with the smallest number of directed edges.
we provide an algorithm that constructs a 2-realizer on a circuit-switching d-cube in d2d steps, which is optimal in both the number of steps and the size of the 2-realizer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the realization problem on the d-cube is not only solvable, but is solvable with an algorithm whose complexity is polynomial in d, the dimension of the d-cube.
, in the worst case, the number of directed edges required for realizing a permutation on a d-cube is at most d2d.
, in the circuit-switched setting, the number of directed edges needed in a 2-realizability of a permutation can be made arbitrarily small, as long as the permutation is given explicitly.
